This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/kernel/runtime-services/index.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via ISecurityService (symbol, a top-level interface))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fc08f7a1613a91ddf717941c6e9348dde19a7de3` — the merge of head `082e8bf80665184fce72aa9120aaea14e3b9bcb5` into base `66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fc08f7a1613a91ddf717941c6e9348dde19a7de3 && git checkout fc08f7a1613a91ddf717941c6e9348dde19a7de3
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3 082e8bf80665184fce72aa9120aaea14e3b9bcb5 && git checkout -B drift-repro 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3 && git merge --no-ff 082e8bf80665184fce72aa9120aaea14e3b9bcb5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Head-sha: `d3adb0d1cdbf4bebe67ae162616037ecf1f31d0a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template + packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-write-gate.ts (`assertControlledByParentWrite`, `nullMasterRowWritable`, `bodyEmptiesMasterReference`, `askBodyNamedMaster`, `checkControlledByParentWrite`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts (`ownerMayEdit` resolution), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/permission-evaluator.ts (`hasSuperuserWriteBypass`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/errors.ts (`PermissionDeniedError`, `MasterReferenceMissingError`), docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md (section 3 and the amendments of 2026-10-26, 2026-11-06 and 2026-11-07), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-owner-may-edit.test.ts and packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/controlled-by-parent-optional-master.test.ts (the pins the new text is accepted against), .changeset/30905-cbp-optional-master.md and .changeset/30906-cbp-null-master-write-gate.md (for ③). Cited code read on `origin/main`, which is byte-identical to the merge base for every cited file; `reviewFace` reads the four-path file list as the schema face with the three `hits` above and no rules hit.

Inputs: card #31169 (body; comments 6709432110, 6710037976, 6710851706, 6710876574), card #31180 (body; comments 6710232004, 6710378726), PR #31210 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...d3adb0d1` (4 files, +51/-8, two commits 0fcd5b1b and d3adb0d1), and the 41 check-runs on the head. The PR is a draft on an internal branch (head repo equals base repo), labels `documentation`, `size/s`, `tooling`; no governed-surface path is in the file list, so the review is owed by the schema face alone.

Check-runs on the head at review time: 18 completed success (Auto Label; Check Changeset; Check PR Size; Dogfood Regression Gate; Flag docs affected by code changes; Governed Surface Queue Guard; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · ESLint; Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped · query-options erasure; Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests; PR-body guards; Plan Test Core shards; Spec property liveness; Type Check · source gates; filter), 8 skipped (opt-in and path-filtered jobs), 15 still in progress (Build Core; Build UI Deps; Lint · scoped · slot lookup and corpus; Live E2E UI; Test Core 1/8 to 8/8; Type Check · consumer gates; Type Check · debt ledger; Type Check · workspace). Not waited for. The gate families that judge the `hits` text directly are already green: `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide` run in Type Check · source gates, `check:doc-authoring` in Lint · repo & tooling gates, the changeset declaration lines in Check Changeset and PR-body guards. `check:api-surface` (Type Check · consumer gates) is in progress; it cannot be moved by this diff, see ①.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set: unchanged — right.** No zod schema, type, export, signature or runtime branch is touched; `git diff` shows only string literals and comment text. `Metadata-protocol: none` is the correct kind: nothing an author can write is added, narrowed or re-meant. `Clause-②: no` with no arm is right for the same reason. Spec property liveness is green.
- **Published surface, what actually moves:** (a) the JSDoc of two exported declarations, `ControlledByParentWriteOutcome` and `ISecurityService.checkControlledByParentWrite`, which ship in `dist/*.d.ts`; (b) the `replacement` value of the `SemanticMigration` entry `cbp-optional-master-admitted`, which is registry data read by `os migrate meta` and compiled into `spec-changes.json`; (c) the STEP18 rationale fragment of the same id, rendered into `protocol-upgrade-guide.md`. All three are text a consumer reads, none is a contract a consumer compiles against. Judged right: this is exactly the published-text patch the two cards ask for.
- **Generated artifacts: nothing owed in the PR — right.** `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` is gitignored and regenerated on install and at build (`gen:migration-registry` in `prepare`, `build`, `test`, `typecheck`); `spec-changes.json` and `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` are gitignored and pinned by `check:spec-changes` / `check:upgrade-guide`, which are green on this head. The tracked `packages/spec/api-surface/*.json` reports carry no docblock text and do not even name `checkControlledByParentWrite`, so a JSDoc-only diff cannot change them; the PR leaves them untouched, correctly.
- **Pins:** a grep of the head tree for the three replaced sentences finds no test, snapshot or doc quoting them; the only hit is the new template sentence itself. The dev's claim on this point holds.
- **Merge state:** `origin/main` has moved past the merge base (620b6e6d to d57be872) and touches `registry.ts.template` in a different STEP18 fragment (marketplace manifest entries); a merge-tree dry run of the head onto `origin/main` is clean. None of the cited gate, ADR, contract or test files changed between the merge base and `origin/main`, so the judgment below is against the live tree.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/31169-cbp-optional-master-entry-write-text.md` declares `'@objectstack/spec': patch` and carries both line-initial declarations, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, identical to the PR body's. Right: a `none` kind on a released package takes `patch`; the text ships in the npm package (`dist`, `spec-changes.json`, `protocol-upgrade-guide.md` are in `files[]`), so `skip-changeset` would be wrong and is not used. No arm, no BREAKING banner, no ADR-0087 marker owed. Check Changeset and PR-body guards are green on the head. One changeset for the fold is what claim 6710378726 ordered (fold gate ②). Clause-②: no.

### ③ Boundary flags

Read off os-dev-report 6710851706 on #31169, the PR body's Acceptance notes, and the two claims.

1. **`registry.ts.template` outside the claimed file surface** (dev flag; rule-3 bounded exemption). Answered: claim amendment 6710876574 adds the path to claim 6710037976. The hunk is the one stale sentence about the one entry, in the family both triage audits (6709432110, 6710232004) name. Closed.
2. **`.changeset/30905-cbp-optional-master.md` still says "Writes are unchanged ... still refused with 422"** (dev `out_of_scope_findings`, PR Acceptance notes). Confirmed on `origin/main`: that pending changeset's plugin-security bullet ends with the stale sentence, and `30906-cbp-null-master-write-gate.md` in the same pending set states the write rule, so one release's CHANGELOG will carry both. It is outside both cards' surfaces, and a pending changeset is an ordinary tracked file, not a landed record. Escalated to the seat as a should-fix follow-up, not a blocker on this PR: either a one-line edit of that bullet folded here before landing (same family, same package, same `patch` level unaffected), or a follow-up card in the #31094/#31169/#31180 family. Not a FAIL: the published text this PR owns is right, and the release notes' write-side statement already exists.
3. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` NOT MEASURED locally** (needs every package's `dist`). CI's: Build Core is in progress at review time. The Tier rule that lands a PR waits on every check green; this record does not pre-empt that and does not need to.
4. `open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, `premise_still_valid: true`, two commits one per card with one `Fixes` line each as the fold claim ordered. No other flag.

### ④ Design judgment

Every sentence the new text states about the write gate was read against `assertControlledByParentWrite` and what it calls, and tried against the pinned scenarios.

**packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts (card #31180).**

The `allow` bullet of `ControlledByParentWriteOutcome` — holds, sentence by sentence:
- "the detail opts in with `sharing.controlledByParent.ownerMayEdit: true`": the leg tests `rel.ownerMayEdit`, which `security-plugin-cbp-relation.ts` resolves as `optedIn && hasOwnerColumn` (an opt-in without an `owner_id` column resolves false and is reported once). The bullet's "the record's stored `owner_id`" carries the column requirement; consistent.
- "its owner leg admits the principal in place of the walk": on the leg's success the gate `return`s before `assertControlledByParentChainEditable`; true.
- "the context is not on behalf of another user": `!opCtx?.context?.onBehalfOf?.userId`. For the served member `opCtx.context` is the caller's context on both passes of a delegated call, so a delegated context skips the leg on the agent's and the delegator's pass alike; true.
- "the record's stored `owner_id` is the principal's own `userId`": `detailRow[OWNER_COLUMN] != null && String(detailRow[OWNER_COLUMN]) === String(context.userId)`; true, and a row with no owner admits nobody.
- "the principal can READ the master the record names": `readUnlessRefused` wrapping `this.readRowById(rel.master, masterId, context)`, admitted only when not refused and the row is non-null; the leg is reachable only when `masterId != null` (an empty optional master was answered earlier by the owner rule, an empty required one by the 422 branch), so "the master the record names" is exact.
- "so no leg asks EDIT on that master or any master above it": the walk is not entered; `askBodyNamedMaster([masterId])` with the served member's body-less `opCtx` returns at once. True for the outcome this type describes. The pin: owner-may-edit test "allow for the owner who reads the master; deny for the same grants without ownership".
- The citation "ADR-0055 §3 as amended 2026-10-26" matches the ADR's amendment line and section-3 note.

The `ISecurityService.checkControlledByParentWrite` docblock — holds with one should-fix:
- "a by-id update": `operation === 'update' && detailRow !== null`; an insert, delete and predicate (`multi`) update never reach the leg (the predicate path returned earlier). True; pinned by the "what the opt-in does NOT widen" describe.
- "by the record's owner (its stored `owner_id` is the caller's own `userId`), not on behalf of another user": as above; true.
- "that does not empty an optional master": `!(rel.optional && bodyEmptiesMasterReference(opCtx.data, rel.fk))`; true, and the ADR's 2026-11-07 amendment says the opt-in does not cover an emptying body. Pinned by "emptying a master asks EDIT on the master it leaves ... even under the ownerMayEdit opt-in". A body emptying a REQUIRED master passes this condition but is refused by `askBodyNamedMaster` (422) or by required-field validation; the docblock's "optional" is the right word.
- "needs only READ access to the master the record names, asked of the read door under the caller's own context": `readRowById(rel.master, masterId, context)` under the caller's context; true.
- "Every other caller, and every insert, delete, predicate update and on-behalf-of write, keeps the edit rule": matches the gate and the ADR amendment line word for word.
- "The leg is part of the check, so such an owner who can read the master gets `allow` here as on the update": the served member builds `{ operation: 'update', options: { where: { id } }, context }` and calls the same function; true, pinned.
- **S1 (should-fix): "and walks no chain" over-claims for one by-id update shape.** When the leg's master read passes, the gate runs `askBodyNamedMaster([masterId])` before returning; a body that re-points the row under a different master (`data[fk]` set to another id) makes that call enter `assertControlledByParentChainEditable` on the new master and ask EDIT on it (ADR-0055 2026-10-26 amendment, "What the leg does not change"; pinned by "a body that RE-POINTS the row under another contract the owner only reads is refused"). So an owner's by-id update meeting every listed condition can still walk a chain, the new master's. The served member carries no body, so every outcome this member contracts is still exactly right, and the `allow` bullet's own wording ("no leg asks EDIT on that master or any master above it", the stored master) is exact; the over-claim is confined to the one clause describing the write path a consumer of this member never runs. Fix: "... and walks no chain for the master the record names; a body that re-points the row under another master still asks EDIT on that master, as every body naming a new master does." Not a must-fix: it changes no answer the contract promises and the sentence beside it already scopes the read to "the master the record names".

**packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.cbp-optional-master-admitted.ts (card #31169).** `id`, `surface`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria` unchanged, as the card required. The new `replacement` sentences, each against the gate:
- "an insert that names no master is admitted, and its creator owns the row": the `masterId == null && rel.optional` block returns on `insert`; the owner stamp is the platform's (step 3.5). Pinned by "an insert with no master reference, and one with `account: null`, land owned by the caller". True. The "admitted" is this gate's admission; the detail's own `create` grant still runs before it, which the entry's reader expects of every write.
- "its owner and a holder of Modify All on the detail update or delete a row whose master reference is empty": `nullMasterRowWritable` admits `hasSuperuserWriteBypass` (the `modifyAllRecords` bit, `permission-evaluator.ts`) or a non-null `owner_id` equal to the caller; a delete takes the same block. True; pinned by "the owner updates and deletes it" and "Modify All on the detail updates and deletes it without owning it".
- "everyone else who reaches the write gate, View All included, is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`": `nullMasterOwnerDenied` is a `PermissionDeniedError`, `code = 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`, `statusCode = 403`. "who reaches the write gate" correctly leaves the hidden-row 404 at the read door outside the sentence. True; pinned by "a principal who READS it (View All) and does not own it is refused both".
- "a row with no owner, or on an object that carries no `owner_id` column, is written through Modify All alone": `!rel.ownerColumn` returns false, `owner == null` returns false; true; pinned.
- "An update that empties a named master asks edit access on the master it leaves": the owner leg steps aside for such a body, the walk asks EDIT on the stored master, then `askBodyNamedMaster` returns for an optional master. True; pinned.
- "A required master is unchanged: a row whose stored required master reference is empty is still refused with `422 MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD`": the `masterId == null` branch throws `MasterReferenceMissingError` (`code = 'MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD'`, `statusCode = 422`) for every non-insert; "stored" is the right qualifier, since an insert omitting a required master is handed to required-field validation (400) where `omissionRefusedByValidation`. True, and more precise than the sentence it replaces.
- The header comment names ADR-0055 section 3 as amended and ruling A as the provenance, with PR #31082 as the convenience link beside the read-side citation; it is a source comment, not a runtime string, and the `replacement` string carries no tracker number; `check:doc-authoring` is green. The wording matches the error-handling and error-catalog pages and the 30906 changeset, so the texts agree as the card wanted.

**packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template (STEP18 fragment `cbp-optional-master-admitted`).** "A detail row that names no master is written by its owner and by Modify All on the detail, and refused with 403 for everyone else; only an empty required master reference is still refused with 422." Both clauses hold against the gate as above; the paragraph's subject is the optional master, so "names no master" is read in scope. The summary is at the precision of the ADR's own amendment line ("everyone else `403`"), which is the register this upgrade-guide paragraph writes in; the entry's `replacement` carries the precise form. No finding.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), one escalation (③ item 2).

### ④ Design judgment

**packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, `ISecurityService.checkControlledByParentWrite` docblock.** The reworded clause: "... asked of the read door under the caller's own context, and walks no chain for that master; a body that re-points the row under another master still asks EDIT on that master, as every body naming a new master does."
